subject: pharmacology
title: Cytotoxic Anticancer II: Platinum Compounds, Cisplatin Nephrotoxicity, Ototoxicity and Emetogenicity

steps.tx: **Platinum compounds** are alkylator like rather than true alkylators: cisplatin, carboplatin and oxaliplatin aquate inside cells and weld intrastrand DNA crosslinks (1,2 dGpG principally) that bend the helix into repair machinery alarms, killing in any phase with characteristic organ signatures replacing marrow as the dose ceiling for two of the three. Germ cell, ovarian, bladder, lung, colorectal and head and neck regimens divide among them by those signatures.
steps.say: Three platinums, three organ ceilings; choose by kidney, marrow or nerve tolerance.

left.title: Shared mechanism
points: No cross resistance fully with alkylators

steps.tx: **Cisplatin nephrotoxicity** is proximal and distal tubular injury by cumulative dose, prevented (never treated) by chloride rich forced saline diuresis before and after, magnesium and potassium repletion by protocol, mannitol in high dose traditions, and avoidance of aminoglycoside partners; creatinine clearance thresholds reassign patients to carboplatin instead. The kidney injury is the price list that built carboplatin's entire career.
steps.say: You prevent cisplatin kidneys with salt water and magnesium; you never treat your way back.

nodes.label: Creatinine clearance, hearing and neuropathy baselined
Forced saline diuresis before and after dose
Magnesium and potassium repleted by protocol

steps.tx: **Ototoxicity** writes cisplatin's paediatric tragedy: irreversible high frequency sensorineural hearing loss beginning beyond speech frequencies and descending, cumulative and worse in children, monitored by audiometry where protocols demand and fenced by dose caps and carboplatin substitution in the youngest. Peripheral neuropathy (stocking glove, cumulative) and Raynaud phenomena queue behind the ear in the chronic ledger.
steps.say: Cisplatin deafens from the top frequencies down, children first; audiograms are dose instruments.

left.title: Ototoxicity facts
points: High frequency loss first, speech frequencies later

right.title: Mitigation habits
points: Baseline and serial audiometry in paediatrics
Sodium thiosulfate in defined paediatric settings

steps.tx: **Highly emetogenic** is cisplatin's third crown: over 90 percent vomiting untreated, acute (serotonin, day one) and delayed (substance P, days 2 to 5) phases demanding the antiemetic lesson's full triple or quadruple prophylaxis (NK1 antagonist, 5HT3 antagonist, dexamethasone, with or without olanzapine) scheduled rather than rescued. Breakthrough failure here teaches patients to fear cycle two more than cancer, making antiemetic precision an adherence drug.
steps.say: Cisplatin vomiting has two phases and four drug answers; schedule them, never chase them.

left.title: Emesis phases
points: Anticipatory: conditioned, prevention by early control

right.title: Prophylaxis architecture
points: NK1 antagonist plus 5HT3 antagonist plus dexamethasone
Delayed phase cover continued at home
Rescue and regimen revision after breakthrough

steps.tx: **Carboplatin** trades cisplatin's kidney, ear and emesis ceilings for marrow (thrombocytopenia principal) and is dosed by renal function arithmetic, the Calvert formula (dose equals target AUC times GFR plus 25), oncology's most used equation. Hypersensitivity reactions accumulate with lifetime exposure (cycle 8 onward vigilance, desensitisation protocols), a platinum allergy career distinct from first dose reactions.
steps.say: Carboplatin is dosed by an equation and allergies arrive by the eighth cycle, not the first.

left.title: Calvert dosing
points: GFR estimation method changes the dose really

right.title: Hypersensitivity career
points: Risk climbs after 6 to 8 lifetime cycles

steps.tx: **Oxaliplatin** owns colorectal cancer (FOLFOX) and a two faced neuropathy: acute cold triggered paraesthesia and jaw tightness within hours (calcium channel mediated, cold avoidance counselled, infusion prolongation softens) and chronic cumulative sensory neuropathy that caps total therapy and recovers slowly. Its marrow and emesis are moderate, kidneys largely spared, and calcium magnesium infusions failed their neuropathy trials while duloxetine treats established pain.
steps.say: Oxaliplatin nerves tingle with cold today and numb cumulatively tomorrow; both write the orders.

left.title: Acute neuropathy
points: Cold triggered paraesthesia and throat tightness

right.title: Chronic neuropathy
points: Stop and go strategies (OPTIMOX) spare nerves

steps.tx: **Platinum resistance** frame the examination synthesis: nucleotide excision repair capacity, glutathione conjugation and copper transporter trafficking decide tumour sensitivity; germ cell tumours' exquisite cisplatin cure (BEP regimens) versus ovarian and lung partial answers map that biology clinically. Non cross resistance with taxanes and antimetabolites is why platinum doublets anchor so many first line regimens.
steps.say: Testicular cancer is platinum biology's triumph; repair capacity writes every other tumour's partial answer.

left.title: Sensitivity biology
points: Germ cell tumours: cure with cisplatin combinations
BRCA and homologous repair defects sensitise

right.title: Regimen architecture
points: Platinum doublets across lung and ovarian first lines
FOLFOX and FOLFIRI sequences in colorectal

steps.tx: **Electrolyte wasting** is cisplatin's quiet chronic signature: renal magnesium wasting persisting years, potassium and calcium dragged behind it, presenting as cramps, tetany or arrhythmia long after therapy and requiring oral magnesium discipline. Survivorship clinics inherit these ledgers (kidney, ear, nerve, magnesium) which is why the baseline tests before cycle one are really survivorship documents written in advance.
steps.say: Cisplatin wastes magnesium for years; the baseline bloods are survivorship's first page.

nodes.label: Tubular injury wastes magnesium and potassium
Cramps, tetany or arrhythmia months later
